History

The desktop vaporizer was defined by the Storz & Bickel Volcano, introduced in 2000 and the benchmark for the category ever since. The Volcano Classic is a purely electromechanical machine: an analog dial, a heater, and an air pump, with no screen or app. It filled a detachable balloon, called a bag, with vapour, and the vapour stayed fresh in the balloon for up to 8 hours according to the maker. The later Volcano Hybrid added a digital display, faster heat-up, app and Bluetooth control, and a whip tube for direct draw alongside the balloon. Over time the same basic form was copied, adapted, and refined by many makers, so the record today covers a family of closely related objects rather than a single patented shape. Museums, trade guides, and manufacturer manuals preserve the steps of that change, and the sources cited at the end of this record give the reader places to check each stage. The history matters because it explains why the parts are arranged the way they are: each feature survives because it solved a practical problem for the people who used the supply every day. The form changed slowly, through small improvements in materials and manufacturing rather than sudden reinvention, and each improvement can be traced in the sources cited at the end of this record. What stayed constant was the job itself, and what changed was how reliably, how evenly, and how durably that job could be done with ordinary materials and ordinary tools.

The supply in detail

The the desktop vaporizer works by mains power heats air in a large aluminium heat exchanger, and an air pump pushes that hot air through a filling chamber of ground herb into a detachable balloon, or through a whip tube. It is made from aluminium heat exchanger, stainless-steel filling chamber, food-grade balloon material, mains-powered heater and air pump, and a common example measures about 200 mm tall, 200 mm diameter base, 100 w heater, balloon about 3 litres when filled. The parts fit together in a fixed order, and each part has one job: to hold the material, to apply the mechanism, or to carry the result to the user. Because the parts are simple and the mechanism is mechanical or thermal rather than electronic in its basic form, the supply can be understood by inspection, measured with a ruler, and checked by the arithmetic in this record. The variants listed in the specification show how makers change size, material, and detail while keeping the same working principle, and the scale variants at the end of this record show the same design at pocket, standard, and workshop sizes.

Parts and variants

Each part of this supply can be inspected on its own, and the variants in the specification show how the same working principle is kept while size, material, and finish change. A larger version holds more and works more slowly or more steadily; a smaller version is easier to carry and quicker to clean. Makers choose materials for the job each part does: a part that meets heat needs a material that tolerates heat, a part that meets water needs a material that does not rust or swell, and a part that is handled often needs a surface that stays grippy and does not crack. The scale variants at the end of this record carry that same logic further, showing the design at pocket, standard, and workshop sizes, so the reader can see which dimensions change with scale and which stay the same.

Spec

Materials: Aluminium heat exchanger; stainless-steel filling chamber and screens; food-grade balloon material; mains-powered heater and air pump

Dimensions: About 200 mm tall x 200 mm diameter base; 100 W convection heater; Easy Valve balloon holds about 3 litres when filled

Mechanism: Pure convection in the Classic: heated air passes through the herb and carries vapour into the balloon; the Hybrid adds conduction and a whip; temperature range 130 C to 230 C (266 F to 446 F) on nine dial levels

Use: Grind medium-fine, fill the chamber loosely, preheat until the temperature settles, attach the balloon, run the fan until the balloon is firm, detach it, and inhale through the valve mouthpiece

Care: Empty the chamber after use; replace balloons when worn; clean the filling chamber and screens; wipe the housing; keep the air intake clear

Variants: Volcano Classic (analog dial, balloon only); Volcano Hybrid (digital display, balloon plus whip, app control); other desktop whip and balloon models

Science proof

A desktop vaporizer is a forced-air convection system. Mains electricity heats a large aluminium block, the heat exchanger, which stores thermal energy and holds a steady temperature while air passes over it. The air pump drives room air through that block, so the air leaves at the set temperature, then flows through the filling chamber where it gives up heat to the herb and picks up vapour. Because the herb never touches the heater, the temperature the herb sees is the temperature of the air, which is why the result repeats from session to session. The balloon is a simple reservoir: vapour collects in it, cools slightly as it waits, and the valve mouthpiece releases vapour only when the user draws. Filling volume is airflow rate times fill time, and the heater energy is power times time. The large heat exchanger is the reason a desktop unit holds temperature better than a small portable: its thermal mass resists the cooling effect of each draw of air. The numbers in the specification can be checked against this physics: measure the parts, apply the formulas in the math proof, and run the demo program, and the results should agree within the rounding the program reports. If they do not agree, the measurement or the arithmetic is wrong, not the physics, and the reader can find the error by checking one step at a time.

Math proof

The demo uses two simple products. First, heat-up energy is heater power times time: 100.0 watts times 180.0 seconds, which the program reports in joules and in watt-hours after dividing by 3600. Second, the filled balloon volume is airflow times fill time: 4.0 litres per minute times 45.0 seconds divided by 60 gives the filled volume in litres, and dividing that by the balloon volume of 3.0 litres gives the fill fraction. Both numbers come from the specification in this record, and the program prints them with units so the reader can repeat the arithmetic by hand. The computation is run twice and the SHA-256 digests of both runs are printed, confirming the result is deterministic. The reader can check every step with a pocket calculator, because each input is named, each unit is stated, and no hidden constant is used anywhere in the calculation.

Use and care

Grind medium-fine, fill the chamber loosely, preheat until the temperature settles, attach the balloon, run the fan until the balloon is firm, detach it, and inhale through the valve mouthpiece Empty the chamber after use; replace balloons when worn; clean the filling chamber and screens; wipe the housing; keep the air intake clear Keep the supply dry when it is stored, keep its working surfaces clean, and replace worn parts such as screens, balloons, or filter tips when they no longer do their job. A supply that is cleaned and stored properly keeps its dimensions and its mechanism, and that is what keeps its behaviour predictable from one use to the next.

Legal note

Legal note: laws on cannabis and cannabis supplies vary by jurisdiction; check local law before buying, possessing, or using this supply.

Sources

  • Australian Vaporizers — Volcano Vaporizer FAQ — https://www.australianvaporizers.com.au/pages/volcano-vaporizer-faq — The Volcano is the desktop balloon vaporiser from Storz & Bickel, the benchmark since 2000; set a temperature, the unit heats herb with hot air, and a fan inflates a balloon full of vapour; the Classic has a dial and balloon-only delivery, the Hybrid adds a digital display, faster heat-up, app control, and a whip.
  • Vaposhop — Volcano Classic Onyx Edition — https://www.vaposhop.com/products/volcano-classic-onyx-edition — The Volcano Classic uses pure convection and a powerful air pump to fill Easy Valve balloons with vapor; the analog dial sets temperatures from 130-230 C (266-446 F); it has a 100 Watt convection heating source with a large aluminium heat exchanger; heat-up takes 1 to 3 minutes.

demo.code:
"""Demo: desktop vaporizer balloon fill — The Desktop Vaporizer."""
import hashlib
def compute():
    heater_w = 100.0; heatup_s = 180.0; airflow = 4.0; fill_s = 45.0; balloon_l = 3.0; temp_c = 190.0
    heatup_energy_j = heater_w * heatup_s
    fill_min = fill_s / 60.0
    filled_l = airflow * fill_min
    fill_fraction = filled_l / balloon_l
    fills_per_hour = 3600.0 / fill_s
    return {"heatup_energy_J": round(heatup_energy_j, 1), "heatup_energy_Wh": round(heatup_energy_j / 3600.0, 2), "filled_volume_L": round(filled_l, 2), "balloon_volume_L": balloon_l, "fill_fraction": round(fill_fraction, 2), "target_temp_C": temp_c}
def main():
    a = compute(); b = compute()
    sa = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(a.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
    sb = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(b.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
    for key in ["heatup_energy_J", "heatup_energy_Wh", "filled_volume_L", "balloon_volume_L", "fill_fraction", "target_temp_C"]:
        print(f"{key}: {a[key]}")
    print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {sa}")
    print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {sb}")
    print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if sa == sb else 'MISMATCH'}")
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

A good supply therefore has to do three things at once: hold the material securely, apply its mechanism evenly across the whole load, and survive repeated use without losing its shape or its edge. """The Desktop Vaporizer — full working program.

Computes the same quantities as the record demo (desktop vaporizer balloon fill),
as a documented module with a class and a run() method.
Run: python3 program.py
"""
import hashlib
import math


class SupplyCalculator:
    """Calculator for The Desktop Vaporizer."""

    def compute(self):
        """Return the computed quantities as a dict."""
        heater_w = 100.0; heatup_s = 180.0; airflow = 4.0; fill_s = 45.0; balloon_l = 3.0; temp_c = 190.0
        heatup_energy_j = heater_w * heatup_s
        fill_min = fill_s / 60.0
        filled_l = airflow * fill_min
        fill_fraction = filled_l / balloon_l
        fills_per_hour = 3600.0 / fill_s
        return {"heatup_energy_J": round(heatup_energy_j, 1), "heatup_energy_Wh": round(heatup_energy_j / 3600.0, 2), "filled_volume_L": round(filled_l, 2), "balloon_volume_L": balloon_l, "fill_fraction": round(fill_fraction, 2), "target_temp_C": temp_c}

    def run(self):
        """Compute twice, print named results and SHA-256 digests."""
        a = self.compute()
        b = self.compute()
        sa = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(a.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
        sb = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(b.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
        for key in sorted(a):
            print(f"{key}: {a[key]}")
        print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {sa}")
        print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {sb}")
        print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if sa == sb else 'MISMATCH'}")
        return a


if __name__ == "__main__":
    SupplyCalculator().run()
